sentences.text: The partial proximal parietal bone of Zuniceratops has an inverted "T" shape, similar to that of Protoceratops.
The frill of Zuniceratops was a thin, wide structure resembling a shield.
The snout of Zuniceratops was long and low, similar to that of chasmosaurines.
This dinosaur was discovered in 1996 by an eight-year-old boy named Christopher James Wolfe.
Larger fossils show double-rooted teeth, indicating that teeth became double-rooted with age.
Wolfe and James Kirkland first described Zuniceratops in 1998.
The name Zuniceratops is derived from the Zuni people of New Mexico and Arizona, who named the basin where fossils were found, and the Latinized Greek term ceratops meaning "horned face".
Zuniceratops was a herbivore like other ceratopsians and was probably an animal that lived in herds.
Researchers believe that the brow horns of Zuniceratops would have grown much larger with age.
The genus Zuniceratops contains a single known species, Zuniceratops christopheri.

Due to its combination of primitive and advanced features, Zuniceratops is classified as the sister taxon to the family Ceratopsidae, possibly grouped with the Asian ceratopsian Turanoceratops in a group named Ceratopsomorpha by Kirkland and Wolfe.
Zuniceratops lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now New Mexico, United States.
Zuniceratops lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 94 million years ago during the Turonian, in what is now North America.
The time range for Zuniceratops is the Turonian stage, from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
